notes: Two parallel naming conventions live here: the user-facing camelCase set (createOrderRequest, getOrderResponse, etc.) and the .NET-namespaced internal DTOs (eToro.Trading.DistributedServices.WebApi.API.DTO.Requests.*). The lowercase ones are what API users typically call; the namespaced ones describe internal request shapes.
Heavy field-name casing inconsistency: instrumentId vs instrumentID vs InstrumentId vs InstrumentID across schemas. Plan on using #[serde(rename = ...)] generously.
ALL price/amount/rate fields are float in spec — use rust_decimal::Decimal in production code, never f32/f64
orderType is 'MKT' or 'LMT' (string enum); executionType is 'GTC' or 'IOC' (string enum). Model as Rust enums with #[serde(rename_all)].
BUT some schemas (Order, OrderForOpen, OrderForClose, OrderForOpenInfoResponse) use INTEGER orderType/executionType — same concept, different wire format per endpoint
Position has 35 fields — the heaviest non-portfolio object schema. Many will be missing/nullable in practice; model defensively.
Mirror (copy-trading) has 26 fields and lots of obsolete/internal state — read the descriptions carefully; many fields are marked Obsolete.
TradeDirection (Long/Short), TradeType (Open/Close) are integer-encoded with string-named variants — wire format is the integer index
